front.title: Why the Mobile User Plane Is the Way It Is

abstract.t:
The Mobile User Plane (MUP) architecture transforms session information from a mobile service system into routing information, so that ordinary routing nodes can take on the roles of user plane anchors and intermediate points. The architecture document that defines MUP is a normative text: it defines concepts, route types, and resolution procedures, but it does not explain why they are the way they are. This companion reader supplies that "why", outside the normative text.
The technical content follows one worked example end to end, with concrete prefixes, SIDs, and tunnel endpoint identifiers, and follows the architecture document throughout. The explanations are organized around a small set of shapes that recur in the design: places deliberately left undecided, meaning that arises only when two pieces of information meet, and a strict separation between a name and the thing it points at. The Introduction gives these shapes a name borrowed from Zen, once, and then lets them do their work quietly.
This document is not normative. It defines no protocol and no encoding.
